h: Tips for a top day on the little line
p: Kingsway is a smart place to start your ride if you're already down at the southern end of the seafront, near the leisure centre and the boating lake. It tends to be a little calmer than the town centre end, which makes boarding with buggies, grandparents and excited toddlers that bit easier.

Before the train arrives, take a moment to watch it come in across the viaduct over the boating lake. It's a lovely sight and a brilliant photo opportunity, so have the camera ready. Railway fans will want to know what's pulling the train that day, and younger children usually just want to wave at the driver, which is all part of the fun.

On board, the carriages are small and cosy, so a folded buggy and a light bag make life easier. Sit on the seaward side for the best views of the beach and the Humber, where you might spot big ships heading in and out of the estuary towards Grimsby and Immingham. Some carriages are open, so a coat is a good shout on breezy days.

Make the most of Lakeside at the other end. Little railway fans can see the engines up close, the grown-ups can pop into the tiny Signal Box Inn, and there's room for a walk before heading back. The Cleethorpes Country Park and the dunes around Humberston are nearby too if you fancy stretching your legs.

The railway is a much-loved part of Cleethorpes, and a ride along the front is one of those simple seaside treats that never really gets old, whether you're five or seventy-five. Pair it with a picnic on the beach, a go on the boating lake and fish and chips on the front, and you've got a proper Cleethorpes day sorted.
